sentences.text: The fossil ankle bone is elongate and slender, looking similar to that of modern barn owls.
Ogygoptynx wetmorei is the oldest known owl fossil discovered worldwide.
The genus Ogygoptynx and its only species, Ogygoptynx wetmorei, were named by Rich and Bohaska in 1976 from a single ankle bone found in Late Paleocene deposits in Colorado, USA.
Ogygoptynx wetmorei is the only species within the monotypic family Ogygoptyngidae.
This extinct owl genus lived in North America during the Paleocene epoch, between 60.9 and 57.5 million years ago.
Scientists consider the existence of this species a puzzle regarding early owl evolution.
Researchers note a contrast between the modern ankle structure of this North American owl and primitive forms found in Europe at the same time.
It is debated why similar advanced owls disappear from the North American fossil record for a long time after this species.
